artists.biography:
Splashgirl (initiated 2003 in Oslo, Norway) is a Norwegian jazz ensemble comprising the three young musicians Andreas Stensland Løwe (piano and electronics), Jo Berger Myhre (doublebass and tone generator) and Andreas Lønmo Knudsrød (drums, percussion and sounds), playing original music.

Since 2007, Splashgirl has released four highly acclaimed albums Doors. Keys. (2007), Arbor (2009), Pressure (2011) and Field Day Rituals (2013), has played a great number of concerts in Europe, USA and Japan, and collaborated with musicians like Sidsel Endresen, Jan Bang, Eyvind Kang, Mari Kvien Brunvoll, Randall Dunn and Timothy Mason.

perplexity.description:
Released in 2018 on Hubro Music, Sixth Sense is the sixth studio album by Norwegian jazz ensemble Splashgirl. The album continues the group’s signature blend of jazz, ambient, and experimental soundscapes, characterized by atmospheric piano, textured double bass, and nuanced percussion. Splashgirl—comprised of Andreas Stensland Løwe, Jo Berger Myhre, and Andreas Lønmo Knudsrød—further explores the interplay between acoustic instruments and electronic elements, crafting a contemplative and immersive listening experience. Tracks such as “Carrier,” “Broken,” and the title track “Sixth Sense” showcase their refined approach to mood and dynamics, balancing minimalism with subtle complexity.

Sixth Sense stands as a mature chapter in Splashgirl’s discography, following acclaimed releases like Arbor (2009) and Pressure (2011). The album was well-received for its cohesive atmosphere and innovative use of space and texture, reinforcing the group’s reputation as leading figures in contemporary Nordic jazz. While not a commercial blockbuster, it garnered positive critical attention for its introspective sound and artistic consistency, further cementing Splashgirl’s status within the Hubro roster and the broader European jazz scene.
